VAL-SKEL-015.description: Resize (120x40 → 80x24 → 120x40) during active token streaming must NOT drop tokens, duplicate rows, lose composer focus, or break the cancel key binding.

UpdateSize.finding: UpdateSize holds mutex and only mutates width, height, tooSmall, and phase. It does NOT touch streamLines, focusedLane, selectedIndex, or agents. This is the correct SIGWINCH-safe design - resize events are idempotent with respect to application state.

ApplyAskStreamUpdate.finding: Tokens are appended to streamLines via append(). Tokens are never removed or overwritten on resize. The method holds c.mu during all state mutations. Delta tokens are appended to the last line if it starts with 'assistant: ', otherwise a new line is created. This correctly preserves token continuity across resizes.

Cancel.finding: Cancel() calls ctxCancel() which cancels the context passed to the stream source. The canceler function is stored separately and called explicitly. Resize does not affect the cancel mechanism because UpdateSize does not touch the runtime or its cancel context.

tests.name: TestSigwinchMidStream_TokensNotDropped
tests.verifies: All emitted tokens retained in streamLines across 120x40→80x24→120x40 resize sequence
tests.mechanism: Slow token emission (5ms/token), resize mid-stream, verify all 10 tokens present in rendered text

tests.name: TestSigwinchMidStream_NoDuplicateRows
tests.verifies: No duplicated content in Detail lane after resize
tests.mechanism: Apply half updates, resize to 80x24, count 'alpha' occurrences in detail lane ≤1

tests.name: TestSigwinchMidStream_FocusPreserved
tests.mechanism: Set FocusedLane(1), resize to 80x24, resize back to 120x40, verify FocusedLane() == 1 at each step

tests.name: TestSigwinchMidStream_CancelKeyBindingWorks
tests.verifies: Cancel() works immediately after resize during active streaming
tests.mechanism: Wait for stream in-flight, resize to 80x24, call rt.Cancel(), verify canceler called and status shows 'cancelled' or '⊘'

tests.name: TestSigwinchMidStream_RenderNoCorruption
tests.verifies: No overlapping cells or orphaned box-drawing chars at each resize step
tests.mechanism: Render at 120x40 (streaming), resize to 80x24 (streaming), collect remaining updates, resize back to 120x40. assertNoOverlap + assertNoOrphanedBoxDrawing at each step.

tests.name: TestSigwinchMidStream_NoGoroutineLeak
tests.verifies: Goroutine count stable after resize + stream completion
tests.mechanism: Baseline goroutine count, stream + resize, drain updates, Stop(), GC sleep, verify delta ≤2

test_coverage.assessment: COMPREHENSIVE — all VAL-SKEL-015 requirements covered with both unit tests and tuistory snapshot evidence

test_fixture_fix.rationale: os.Signal(nil) returns nil on all platforms, causing Signal() to return an error on macOS (darwin). syscall.Signal(0) is the standard cross-platform null-signal check that returns success if the process is alive.
test_fixture_fix.impact: Enables the per-test-daemon fixture to boot reliably on macOS, required for tuistory-driven SIGWINCH tests. This is a prerequisite for all M3 integration tests.
test_fixture_fix.assessment: CORRECT — minimal, targeted fix that resolves the macOS process-liveness detection issue without changing behavior on other platforms

architectural_notes.detail: The SIGWINCH resilience is already correct in the existing CockpitScreen implementation. UpdateSize does not mutate streamLines, focusedLane, or selectedIndex. The new tests serve as regression protection rather than fixing a bug. This is the correct approach - the design was already sound.

The tests use MockTerminal-based unit testing without the per-test-daemon fixture (no live foxctl web serve). The tuistory snapshots in .factory/validation/tui-sigwinch/ were captured using the standalone cockpit_sigwinch_demo binary. This is appropriate for SIGWINCH testing because the resize behavior is determined by CockpitScreen state management, not by daemon interaction.

The testfixture fix (2c53f5a6) resolves a macOS-specific issue where os.Signal(nil) always returns nil, causing Signal() to fail. This is a pre-existing issue in the fixture infrastructure, not specific to SIGWINCH, but required for tuistory integration tests.

criterion_1_no_token_drops.code_path: cockpit.go:ApplyAskStreamUpdate → streamLines append; cockpit.go:UpdateSize does not touch streamLines
criterion_1_no_token_drops.mechanism: Tokens are appended to streamLines via append(). UpdateSize does not modify streamLines. The resize sequence (120x40→80x24→120x40) does not affect the slice. Test verifies all 10 emitted tokens present in final stream text.

criterion_2_no_duplicate_rows.mechanism: ApplyAskStreamUpdate appends tokens to the last line or creates a new line. It does not duplicate existing lines. Resize does not re-render streamLines content. Test counts 'alpha' occurrences in detail lane ≤1 after resize.

criterion_3_focus_preserved.code_path: cockpit.go:UpdateSize does not touch focusedLane; cockpit.go:SetFocusedLane/FocusedLane for accessor
criterion_3_focus_preserved.mechanism: UpdateSize only sets width/height/tooSmall/phase. focusedLane is accessed via FocusedLane() getter. Resize does not change focus.

criterion_4_cancel_works_after_resize.mechanism: Cancel calls ctxCancel() on the runtime's context. UpdateSize does not affect the runtime or its context. Test verifies canceler called and status shows 'cancelled' or '⊘' immediately after resize.
